CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this package is

manifoldsR is a thin R wrapper over Rust. Every algorithm (UMAP, tSNE, densMAP, den-SNE, PHATE, PacMAP, diffusion maps, EVoC, k-means) lives in external crates (manifolds-rs, ann-search-rs, evoc-rs, bixverse-rs). The Rust code in src/rust/src/ is a translation layer only: it parses R lists into the crates’ parameter structs, dispatches fp32/fp64, and converts matrices. If an algorithm needs a real change, it belongs upstream in the crate, not here.

Commands

rextendr::document()          # rebuild Rust + regenerate R/extendr-wrappers.R + roxygen
devtools::load_all()          # load without reinstalling
devtools::check()             # full R CMD check
tinytest::run_test_file("inst/tinytest/test_umap.R")   # single test file
tinytest::test_package("manifoldsR")                   # all tests

DEV_BUILD=1 (env var, read by tools/config.R) keeps src/rust/target and the shared cargo registry warm and drops LTO. Use it for iteration; never for benchmarking or a release. There is no debug profile. The package always builds --release.

Rust-only checks are faster via cargo directly:

cargo check --manifest-path src/rust/Cargo.toml
cargo clippy --manifest-path src/rust/Cargo.toml

Layout and generated files

  • src/Makevars and src/Makevars.win are generated by configure -> tools/config.R from the .in templates. Edit the templates, never the output.
  • R/extendr-wrappers.R is generated by the document bin (src/rust/document.rs) during the cargo build. Do not edit. Roxygen on the rs_* functions is written as /// doc comments on the Rust side and flows through into this file.
  • .copier-answers.yml marks the files owned by the personal-templates copier template (configure, cleanup, tools/, Makevars.*.in, CI workflows). Changes there get overwritten on the next copier update.

The per-algorithm pattern

Each method repeats the same five-part structure. Follow it exactly when adding one.

  1. params_<algo>() in R/params.R: a wrapper returning a named list of algorithm parameters with match.arg + checkmate::qassert on each.
  2. check<Algo>Params() / assert<Algo>Params() in R/checkmate_extensions.R: the check* function returns TRUE or an error string; the assert* is built with checkmate::makeAssertionFunction().
  3. .prepare_<algo>_params() in R/<algo>.R: merges nn_params with the algorithm params into one flat list, applies data-dependent defaults (e.g. UMAP picks n_epochs from n and the optimiser). Exported but @keywords internal.
  4. <algo>() in R/<algo>.R: the user-facing function. Coerces data frames to matrices, validates, then branches on whether a NearestNeighbours object was supplied: rs_<algo>_from_knn() if yes, rs_<algo>() if no. Both calls are wrapped in tryCatch that rethrows with a prefixed message.
  5. src/rust/src/<algo>.rs: an Internal<Algo>Params<T> struct with a from_r_list() that pulls each key out of a HashMap<&str, Robj> with a fallback default. The corresponding rs_* function goes in src/rust/src/lib.rs and must be registered in the extendr_module! block there.

The flat-list handoff means R and Rust agree on parameter names by convention only. A rename on one side silently falls back to the Rust default on the other. Check both.

Cross-cutting conventions

  • Precision: parse_precision(use_high_precision, nrows) in lib.rs picks fp32 below SAMPLE_THRESHOLD_HIGH_PRECISION (100k samples) and fp64 above, unless the user forces it. Every rs_* embedding function duplicates its body across an fp32 and an fp64 match arm. Keep both in sync.
  • Verbosity: R side accepts TRUE/FALSE or 0L/1L/2L, converted by parse_verbosity() in R/utils.R to an integer passed to Rust as verbose.
  • kNN reuse: generate_knn_graph() returns a NearestNeighbours S3 object holding flat sorted indices/dist plus k and n. Every embedding method accepts it via the knn = argument to skip the search.
  • S3 classes: NearestNeighbours, Evoc, KMeansCluster are all plain lists with a class attribute, constructed in R/classes.R with getters as generics. No S4, no R6.
  • Deprecations go in R/deprecated.R using lifecycle::deprecate_warn().

Tests

tinytest, in inst/tinytest/. Each file sources ./utils_test.R for the shared helpers (check_cluster_separation(), density_preservation(), check_branch_topology()). Tests use synthetic data from rs_data_* with a fixed seed and assert structural/topological properties (cluster separation, density correlation, branch ordering) rather than exact coordinates. Embeddings aren’t bit-reproducible across the fp32/fp64 paths.

misc/workbench.R is a scratch file for benchmarking against phateR, uwot, Rtsne. Not part of the build.
